scope: cross-NUMA performance: same-node controls and writer/reader split across NUMA0/NUMA1

environment.method: One writer process and N reader processes per round, each pinned with taskset to one physical core; 5 s warmup then 30 s measured; the final STAT line reports post-warmup counters and a <=1.6% log-linear latency histogram.

limits: One writer and up to 8 readers, payload 256B, inline/classic, 10k/s and saturated 8-reader.
Warmup is 5 s and measured window 30 s per round; finals are post-warmup deltas.
Latency percentiles are per-round histogram quantiles (<=1.6% bucket error) averaged over rounds.
The host is shared; selected cores were idle at start but not reserved.
Only two NUMA nodes exist; no cross-socket variants beyond NUMA0/NUMA1, and no NUMA interleave policy.
note: 80 rounds (16 configs x 5) all PASS, zero loss. Workers are separate processes pinned with taskset; writer and reader CPU sets are recorded per config.
